newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria stock surge ahead as big losers stabilise.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria stock surge ahead as big losers stabilise.

text.p: Nigeria's all-share stock index made impressive gains on Monday in a continuously surging market, traders said.
It closed at 7538.45 on Monday from 7511.29 last Friday when conglomerate PZ and Nigerian Breweries suffered big price drops.
The two stocks were steady on Monday.
Traders said the same pattern which saw banks, food and beverages as well as petroleum marketers advance strongly in recent weeks still ruled the market.
"Improved results and better prospects are the dominant factors responsible for the gains," one said.
Cadbury and Nigerian Bottling Company each gained 30 kobo to 31.40 naira and 41.30 naira, respectively.
First Bank closed at 12.80 naira, up 30 kobo while UBA bank was at 9.55 naira, up 45 kobo and Union Bank at 11.30 naira, up 10 kobo.
African Petroleum shot to 55.05 naira, adding 35 kobo while National Oil, Total and Unipetrol eached gained 20 kobo to 56.70 naira, 68.70 naira and 71.70 naira, respectively.

Conglomerates also rebounded, led by Lever Brothers at 19.20 naira, a gain of 20 kobo. UAC added one kobo to 10.51 naira. Franco-Nigerian firm CFAO also added one kobo after several months on the slide.
Monday's big loser was Guinness Brewery, down 20 kobo to 7.20 naira.
Nigerian Breweries was unchanged on Monday at 14.50 naira following a 1.45 naira loss last week. PZ Industries also closed steady at 24.50 naira after shedding 2.50 naira last week.

Stakeholders who saw their holding in healthcare firm Smithkline Beecham increase substantially following a merger with Sterling Products last year were responsible for its slump on Monday to 7.30 naira, down by 10 kobo.

Textiles group Afprint finished five kobo down at 2.35 naira on its recent poor result and because of apprehension over the scrapping of duties on imported textiles which analysts said would affect the fortunes of local textile companies.
